title: Account Request Matchmaker & Release-Slot Brokerage
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, auditable mechanism that translates incoming top-account asks and escalations into prioritized roadmap slots or negotiated deferred-scope agreements. The system should run as a lightweight decision layer that outputs (1) recommended release-slot assignment (canary, next sprint, Q-tranche) or (2) a negotiated deferred-scope proposal with credits and delivery runway.

Why: Sales and CS escalations currently flood PM with ad-hoc asks and manual negotiation. Engineering and Product teams lack a shared, repeatable arbitration model tied to measurable signals (ARR, active usage, churn risk, contractual SLAs) and available delivery capacity.

Key concepts and components:
- Impact Score: weighted combination of ARR, growth velocity, churn risk, security/regulatory constraints, and strategic alignment. Weights configurable via UI.
- Release-Slot Brokerage: discrete delivery slots (full-sprint, half-sprint, micro-fix) that can be reserved by top accounts in exchange for credits, prioritized by Impact Score and escalation severity.
- Deferred-Scope Exchange: standard contractable proposal templates (timeline, scope-frac, credits/refunds) to offer when immediate sloting is infeasible.
- Transparency Ledger: an auditable record linking request -> decision -> owner -> rationale for audit/CS escalations.

User stories:
- As a PM, I want a ranked list of top-account asks sorted by impact and delivery cost so I can make consistent roadmap decisions.
- As an AE, I want a deterministic outcome I can present to a customer within 48 hours of escalation.
- As an Eng manager, I want visibility into slot utilization and capacity hedges so sprint planning can account for reserved work.

Acceptance criteria:
1) System produces consistent ranking for a set of 50 historical escalations with >90% alignment to manually approved historical decisions (evaluation dataset in Drive).
2) Frontend exposes a broker UI where PMs can approve or counter-propose a slot or deferred-scope in <= 72 hours.
3) Audit ledger stored in Confluence/Drive with linkable entries and exportable CSV.
4) Integration hooks: create GitHub issue template for accepted slot; add label and milestone mapping (ENG-19184 required).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Speed vs fairness: strict automation reduces turnaround but may miss nuanced strategic context. We'll include manual override metadata and require PM sign-off for any override.
- Revenue vs product quality: offering paid slots must not undermine long-term roadmap integrity; default cap on paid slots per quarter enforced.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical credit currency (engineering points vs commercial credits)? (PM/RevOps sync scheduled)
- How to model multi-tenant requests that touch core infra (higher cost multiplier).

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://redwood.signals/confluence/TopAccountBroker/draft (internal)
- Google Sheet: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Xk-example-historical-escalations (evaluation dataset)
- Figma mockups: https://www.figma.com/file/Example/slot-broker-ui
- GitHub PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/PR-1267

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Score engine prototype (ENG) that computes Impact Score from existing billing and usage signals.
2) Simple broker UI in Console for PM approvals (two-week alpha).
3) Integrations to GitHub and backlog orchestration (auto-create issue + milestone).
4) Pilot with three top accounts for Q2; gather SLA and commercial feedback.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Sales/CS reject automated outcomes. Mitigation: provide SLA-backed manual arbitration path and 48-hour response SLA.
- Risk: Over-commitment of engineering capacity. Mitigation: enforce quarter caps and require Eng sign-off for any slot reservation that exceeds 10% of planned sprint capacity.
